newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues rules on mortgages for individuals.
newsitem.headline: China issues rules on mortgages for individuals.

text.p: China's central bank, the People's Bank of China issued new rules on Tuesday on the issue of mortgage loans making it easier for individuals to purchase houses.
The mortgage loans would be for a maximum period of 20 years, with the loan amount up to 70 percent of the total purchase cost, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Individuals would be allowed to apply for mortgage loans from commercial banks at preferential interest rates lower than those paid on the fixed-asset loans of a similar term, it said.
The interest rate on a five-year loan would be 10.98 percent, equivalent to the current rate on a three-year fixed asset loan, Xinhua quoted a central bank official as saying.
The rate on five to 10-year loans would be 11.70 percent, equivalent to five-year fixed asset loans, he said. Rates on mortgages of more than 10 years can be slightly higher than 11.7 percent.
The loans would be secured by the property purchased or other property, it said.
Individuals can also borrow from public housing funds -- funds into which most employers and employees pay a certain percentage of their salary each month -- at favourable rates, it said.
Most commercial banks had provided a mortgage service to individuals before a ban by the central bank late last year, an official of the China Construction Bank, the main state housing bank, said.
The official ban was aimed to curb market irregularities because many had banks had rushed to launch the new business, she said.
However, housing industry experts said some local banks may have maintained their mortgage business despite the ban.
The Construction Bank suspended its mortgage service but still retained its policy-oriented individual housing loans, or loans made from the public housing funds, the official said.
"The directive means that banks can resume their mortgage business soon," she said, but declined to give further details.
Commercial banks would not be allowed to make mortgage loans to individuals who want to buy high-class or luxury commercial properties, the central bank said.
The mortgage scheme would be launched in 223 cities nationwide on a trial basis, it said.
The central bank has required commercial banks to set aside a total of 10 billion yuan ($1.2 billion) for the mortgage business, it said.
Previously no banks provided a mortgage loan for a period of more than five years.
